sourceRefs.locator: Nature 601, pp. 388–391. Three worked pieces of wood, the metal-tool cuts and Norse depositional context, Table 1 and Fig. 2 on the radiocarbon signal and counting rings to the surviving outside edge. Published online in 2021.
First two paragraphs. Archaeological evidence of Indigenous use over six millennia and Dorset camps on the south shore more than two centuries before the Norse.

note.de: Nachweisbar wurden drei Bäume im Jahr 1021 gefällt. Bearbeitungsspuren und Fundkontext verbinden die Hölzer mit der nordischen Siedlung an einer bereits lange von indigenen Gemeinschaften genutzten Bucht.
note.en: Three trees were demonstrably felled in 1021. Tool marks and archaeological context connect the worked wood with the Norse site on a bay long used by Indigenous communities.
